intro: River Bend is a Lake Austin waterfront pocket off Quinlan Park Road, with older homes on lots from about a third of an acre to an acre and a half. CleanzATX cleans windows here, where water views make glass quality matter.

sections.h2: What River Bend homes are like
paragraphs: River Bend runs along River Bend Street and Drive, off Quinlan Park Road, and it is part of the older waterfront stretch of Lake Austin. The area is also tied to the Baldwins Point and Sleepy Hollow names. Lots range from about 0.3 to 1.5 acres, and prices run from around $1M to $3M. The homes are older than the planned sections of Steiner Ranch, built over many years, and many have been updated or rebuilt. There is no gate and no master association listed. Each property has its own character, and many have large windows facing the lake.
Waterfront owners tend to know exactly how their glass looks, since the lake is the main thing they see.

sections.h2: What River Bend windows deal with
paragraphs: Water is the problem and the point. Lake spray and humidity leave mineral spots, and docks and decks throw splashes against lower windows. Hard water spots here can etch glass if left for years, and we treat them with hard water spot removal at $10 per pane. Afternoon sun reflecting off the water adds glare that shows every streak and film. Mature trees on bigger lots bring pollen from cedar in winter and live oak in spring, along with leaf litter, webs and sometimes bird droppings, which are acidic and can mark glass.
A lake view home often has big, tall windows, and size multiplies every flaw.

Waterfront lots can mean steep drives, narrow roads and limited parking, so we plan each visit and keep to one driveway. Water fed poles reach up to three stories from the ground, which means we never set a ladder on a slope, deck or wet ground. Our pure water comes from a dual RO, four stage system with a DI resin tank, so we do not rely on lake water or your spigot. Inside windows are cleaned by hand, with drop cloths. Older homes may have older frames, so we handle them gently. We group River Bend with Lakeland Park and Hidden Valley, with a usual lead time within two weeks.
A 4,500 sq ft home is about $450 for exterior windows at $0.10 per sq ft. Count on three and a half to four and a half hours outside, and about two hours inside.

faq.q: Do you clean lakefront windows with spray on them?
faq.a: Yes. Lake spray leaves mineral spots that bond to glass. Pure water handles most, and hard water spot removal at $10 per pane handles the stubborn ones. We tell you first if glass looks etched.

faq.q: Do you need to use my dock or boat house?
faq.a: No. We work from the ground with poles and stay away from docks, boats and the shoreline. Please let us know if there are areas you want us to avoid.

faq.q: Can you work on older homes with older frames?
faq.a: Yes. We use soft tools and light pressure around frames and trim, and the poles let us stay off the house. If we see damaged caulk or glazing, we will mention it.

faq.q: What would I pay for a larger lake home?
faq.a: Exterior windows are $10 per window or about $0.10 per sq ft, so a 4,500 sq ft home is about $450. Adding the inside brings River Bend homes to $15 per window. The minimum job is $200.

faq.q: Can you wash my deck and boat house area?
faq.a: Patios and decks are cleaned by hand so they do not get soaked, at $0.18 per sq ft for concrete and $0.25 for pavers with a $250 minimum. We do not work on docks or boats.
